preconditions: a2 (filename) is non-NULL and a2[0] is not the NUL byte; otherwise the function returns -1 immediately without touching this.

this points to a MAS/cube-map loader object whose start is a writable 12-byte magic-header buffer, with writable fields at this+0x10 (file handle), this+0x14 (filename buffer), this+0x114/+0x118/+0x11C/+0x120/+0x128.
For the fallback search, the audio-directory registry is readable: byte_8B5A3C holds dword_8B8E30 entries of stride 0x84.
This is a synchronous blocking file load; the file must be reachable at the direct path or inside one of the registered audio directories.
postconditions: On return 0: the file is open (handle persisted at this+0x10), the 12-byte header at this matched one of aCubemas410/aCubemas400/aCubemas401, a buffer was allocated at this+0x128 of size (field at this+0x118 << 8), and this+0x11C equals that size plus 24.

On return -1: either the input was invalid (no state change), or the magic header did not match (handle at this+0x10 closed, error logged), or the data-buffer allocation failed (handle closed, error logged).
On return -2: the file could not be opened at the direct path or through any registered audio directory; an error message was logged.
side_effects: Copies a2 byte-wise into this+0x14 up to and including the NUL byte.

Opens a file handle via sub_587DB0 with mode literal "rb" (aRb, 0x005BE828) and stores it at this+0x10; on direct-path failure iterates byte_8B5A3C (stride 0x84, count dword_8B8E30), formatting "%s\%s" candidates with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck and retrying the open.
Reads 12 bytes (magic header) into this, then three 4-byte fields into this+0x114, this+0x118 and this+0x120 via ThreadSafeReadWrapper_803f.
Allocates a heap buffer via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper sized (this+0x118 << 8), stores the pointer at this+0x128, reads the payload into it, then adjusts this+0x11C += 24.
On every failure after the handle is open, closes the handle via FileCloseWithLock and logs through sub_53C590; on success the handle remains open for later teardown.
Reads (does not modify) the global audio-directory registry byte_8B5A3C / dword_8B8E30.

external_dependencies.name: file open (sub_587DB0, mode "rb") and close (sub_587D02) via internal compiler_runtime wrappers, fopen-family
string formatting via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck ("%s\%s", "Error opening MAS file %s")

unresolved: Exact byte contents of the three magic-header literals aCubemas410 (0x005DBC08), aCubemas400 (0x005DBBFC) and aCubemas401 (0x005DBBF0) are not confirmed; only IDA symbol names imply a CUBEMAS410/400/401 form.
Semantics of the two header fields read at this+0x114 and this+0x120 are unknown; only the field at this+0x118 feeds the data-size computation.
Purpose of the +24 adjustment to this+0x11C is unknown.
Length and capacity of the filename buffer at this+0x14 are unknown; the copy loop writes bytes until NUL with no length bound visible in this function.
The object class owning this layout is DERIVED (CubeMapMasFileLoader) and not independently proven; ownership of the file handle after a successful load (who closes it) is not resolved here.
The role of global 0x005C2D64 (aSS_3) is unknown; it appears in packet evidence but is not referenced in the raw function body.

Global addresses for the string literals (0x005BE828 'rb', 0x005DBC14 'Error opening MAS file %s', 0x005DBBD4, 0x005DC5E4) are taken from the packet's operation evidence; the reported width of 1 reflects byte-string access, not confirmed symbol sizes.
tests_required: Load a valid cube-map MAS file: expect return 0, handle at this+0x10 open, buffer at this+0x128 non-NULL, this+0x11C == (header field at this+0x118 << 8) + 24.
File with an unrecognized 12-byte header: expect return -1 and the handle at this+0x10 closed.
File present only in a registered audio directory (byte_8B5A3C): expect the fallback search to open it and return 0.
File missing from the direct path and all audio directories: expect return -2 and an error message logged.
NULL or empty filename: expect return -1 with no writes to this.
Allocation failure for the data buffer: expect return -1 and the handle at this+0x10 closed.
